basis: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; visual impairment in 9/10 lacks ocular localization. Constipation in 7/10 alone does not establish gut damage.

decisions.ocular: none: visual impairment in 9/10 may be cerebral; no intrinsic eye or optic nerve injury is established.

basis: Immunodeficiency with mycobacterial susceptibility; anemia in 2/2 accompanies infection without established intrinsic blood injury. Hepatosplenomegaly alone is insufficient.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia in 2/2 during mycobacterial disease does not establish direct blood damage from the immunodeficiency; marrow injury or hemolysis is not documented.

basis: Serine/glycine metabolic defects; encephalopathy and neurodevelopmental impairment predominate in major clinical forms (>30% estimated overall). Benign biochemical subtypes exist.

decisions.neurologic: involved: glycine encephalopathy and serine-deficiency disorders cause direct brain dysfunction; estimated >30% across the clinical umbrella.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disorder with cardiac involvement in 9/9 and anemia in 7/7. Hearing impairment in only one assessed patient does not establish prevalence; CK alone is insufficient.

decisions.otologic: none: hearing impairment in 1/1 assessed patient, within a nine-patient series, is insufficient to establish involvement in at least 30%.

basis: Paralysis originates in ocular motor nuclei or cranial nerves; impaired eye movements alone do not establish intrinsic ocular injury.

decisions.ocular: none: the lesion is in ocular motor nuclei or nerves; eye movement dysfunction does not independently establish disease of the eye.

basis: Defining cleft lip/palate, dental agenesis, hair abnormalities and syndactyly in the reported family. Eyelid injury is not documented; abnormal EEG alone does not establish neurologic damage.

decisions.ocular: none: broad blepharocheilodontic ancestry does not establish an ocular defect in this subtype; hypertelorism alone is insufficient.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: syndactyly is explicitly part of this syndrome's defining phenotype, rather than an incidental skeletal complication.

basis: Craniosynostosis and limb malformations define Pfeiffer syndrome; hearing loss affects ~50%; structural upper airway obstruction affects an estimated 40-60%. Eye/brain injury varies.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: congenital upper airway narrowing from midface hypoplasia commonly causes persistent obstruction, estimated 40-60% across Pfeiffer syndrome.

basis: Steroid sulfatase deficiency causes sterol metabolic dysfunction and ichthyosis. ADHD (30-79%) is a separate associated diagnosis; corneal deposits usually do not impair vision.

decisions.neurologic: none: ADHD at 30-79% is a separately diagnosed association, not established direct neurologic injury; intellectual disability occurs in only 2/35.

basis: Inherited bile-acid regulatory disorder causing liver failure; characteristic vitamin-K-independent coagulopathy, with prolonged PT in 4/4, supports coagulation involvement.

decisions.haematologic: involved: characteristic vitamin-K-independent coagulopathy is part of NR1H4 deficiency; prolonged PT occurs in 4/4 and reflects loss of coagulation function.

basis: Eyelid, lip and dental malformations define the syndrome; conductive hearing impairment and finger syndactyly each occur in 30-79%. Hair and skin findings are occasional.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: finger syndactyly is a direct congenital structural abnormality of the digits, reported in 30-79%; additional locomotor disability is not required.
